solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Give an indication of engine size or diameter

parts.note: the indefinite article gives the single letter A
cc, cubic centimetres, is how engine capacity is stated
taken as written
d is the standard abbreviation for diameter in geometry

explanation.surface: A request for the size of a car's engine, by capacity or cylinder bore.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant or bestow something, as in granting someone permission, is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Chicane — it turns motorsport into difficult race

indicators.note: the turned word and motorsport go inside the rearranged race
a difficult race is a troubled one, so its letters are mixed up
the small word goes round backwards

parts.note: taken as written
F1, Formula One, read as the letters F and I

explanation.surface: A chicane is a twisting section that makes a motor race harder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses it; Formula One's F1 is read as the letters F and I; 'difficult' mixes up race, and 'into' puts the rest inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicane also means trickery or deception, the same as cunning artfulness.

clue.text: TV presenter takes drive around hazardous part of track

indicators.note: the drive word goes around the presenter's name

parts.note: a cover drive is a cricket stroke, so cover can stand for drive
Jonathan Ross is a British television presenter

explanation.surface: A television host takes a car for a spin round a dangerous stretch of circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: A cover drive is a cricket stroke, so drive can stand for cover; 'around' makes it the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A junction where railway lines meet and trains change tracks is a risky section of railway.

clue.text: About to go around at speed

indicators.note: the about word goes round the other

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is about to set off on a lap at high speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like part of 'about to go' but is the abbreviation re, which 'to go around' wraps round at.
explanation.definitionFit: Velocity, as in a rate of knots, is a pace of movement.

clue.text: Crossing control without silver coating

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the control word goes round the rest

parts.note: a dial is a knob or control on a machine
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
something coating a surface is on it

explanation.surface: An instruction about a crossing control knob that lacks a silver plating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A slanting line that cuts across a square from corner to corner is said to be crossing it.

clue.text: At home, out of work? Not strictly true

parts.note: in means at home
ex means out of or formerly
an act is a deed or piece of work

explanation.surface: Claiming to be unemployed and at home is not quite accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imprecise or approximate is not strictly correct.

clue.text: Oval racers — they won't start breaking into property

indicators.note: the broken letters go inside the property word

parts.note: grounds are land belonging to a property

indicators.note: broken letters are rearranged
the first letter is left off

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Racing dogs that refuse to start, breaking into a property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't start' leaves HEY; 'breaking' rearranges it to EYH, put 'into' GROUNDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing dogs run round an oval track at the dog stadium.

clue.text: Less than 100mph prohibited

definitions.meaning: not allowed or unacceptable, as in that's just not acceptable

explanation.surface: A rule that speeds of a hundred miles per hour are banned.
explanation.definitionFit: Two readings: failing to reach a ton (slang for 100mph), and the idiom for something unacceptable.

clue.text: Bands who would kill to have leader given lowest position

indicators.note: the first letter goes down to the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: a slayer is one who kills

explanation.surface: Musical groups willing to murder to see their frontman relegated.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the lowest position is the end, so S moves from front to back.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata or levels laid one over another are bands of material.

clue.text: Slough racing driver grabs lead in race one

indicators.note: the driver's name holds the other letters inside

parts.note: Stirling Moss was a celebrated British racing driver

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: A driver from the English town of Slough takes the lead in the first race.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is also a town west of London, which disguises the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a swamp or bog, as is a marsh or quagmire.

clue.text: Set to work rebuilding one sort of engine

indicators.note: rebuilding the phrase puts its letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A mechanic gets busy reconstructing a motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilding' rearranges the letters of SET TO WORK.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-cycle petrol motor, as used in mopeds and outboards, is a type of engine.

clue.text: Upper class not starting as competitors?

indicators.note: the first letter of the class word is dropped because it fails to start

parts.note: the gentry are the landed people just below the nobility

explanation.surface: A wry question whether toffs who fail to begin a race still count as racers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' removes the G from GENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole field entered for a race, collectively, is the event's list of competitors; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Sound of racing

definitions.meaning: firm or secure, as a door held tight or a person sound asleep

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both firmly fixed (a synonym of sound) and speedy (a synonym of racing).

clue.text: Old lady preferably keeps active as race competitor

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: one word holds the other inside it as a keeper would

parts.note: rather means preferably, as in I would rather
on means working or active, as a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: An elderly woman who would prefer to stay busy takes up racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' signals a container: the active word sits inside the preferably word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs the 26-mile road race is a long-distance race competitor.

clue.text: Game that guard often plays

parts.note: a security guard watching a car park is often guarding against vehicle theft, the very crime this video game is named after

explanation.definitionFit: A best-selling video game series named after the crime of car stealing, which guards try to prevent.

clue.text: Small vehicles circling very old skips

indicators.note: the vehicles go round the other letters

parts.note: carts are small wheeled vehicles

explanation.surface: Go-karts racing round a vintage car that has jumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' puts V and O inside CARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To prance or leap about in a lively way is a synonym of jumping or bounding along.

clue.text: Race for tuned race buggy

indicators.note: buggy software is faulty, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A beach buggy being tuned up to take part in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buggy' looks like a vehicle but signals an anagram of FOR TUNED RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous multi-stage cycling event held each July is a race.

clue.text: Doctor taking pulse, entertained by your sarcasm?

indicators.note: the pulse word is held as a guest inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
a hum is a steady throb or pulse of sound

explanation.surface: A doctor checking a pulse is amused by a patient's cutting remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertained by' means held inside, as a host holds a guest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcasm is one example of deadpan, ironic wit; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Wheel odds on to go very fast

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the betting odds when a race begins
to rocket is to shoot along at great speed

explanation.surface: A wheel that is backed as favourite to spin at great speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothed cog that engages a chain, as on a bicycle, is a type of wheel.

clue.text: See 16
It's intended to stop them and obstruct progress

parts.note: 'em is the clipped form of them
to bar is to block
go means to proceed or advance

explanation.surface: A barrier designed to halt rivals and block their advance.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban on trade is a measure meant to halt commerce.

clue.text: Unsteady? Wrong to say "Go faster!"

parts.note: giddy means dizzy and unsteady on one's feet
up can mean wrong, as in asking what is up

explanation.surface: Someone questions whether it is a mistake to urge a shaky person to speed up.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry used to urge a horse to move on more quickly is an interjection meaning speed up.

clue.text: Run everyone over during race

indicators.note: the other letters sit within the race abbreviation

parts.note: GP stands for Grand Prix, a motor race
all means everyone
o is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A driver overtakes every rival in the course of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' signals a container; GP is the usual shorthand for a Grand Prix.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's fastest pace, or a quick sprint, is a run.

clue.text: Reportedly a drive's come up

indicators.note: says this phrase is heard as spoken rather than read

parts.note: to drive a ball is to send it, so the phrase is spoken as a send; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A rumour that a drive has turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: Drive and send are both to propel something forward; the 's is no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb or rise is to go upward, the same as to rise up.

clue.text: Harness tangled by feet, gathered by sailor

indicators.note: the sailor word gathers the other letters in, holding them inside

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor

indicators.note: tangled words are twisted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rope harness caught round a seaman's feet and pulled in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangled' scrambles by feet, and 'gathered by' places the result inside the sailor word.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat strap holding a driver in place is a kind of harness.

clue.text: Having emptied fuel, individual raced

indicators.note: removing the inside of the word leaves only its outside letters

parts.note: own means individual or particular to oneself

explanation.surface: A driver who has run the tank dry has nonetheless competed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having emptied' leaves FL from fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone very quickly, as by air, is a past participle like sped or rushed.

clue.text: See 14
River Island clothing is revolting

indicators.note: the island letters dress the turned word, going round it
revolting is turning over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fashions sold at the River Island store are said to be dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: River Island is a British high-street clothing chain, which hides both the definition and the container indicator 'clothing'; 'revolting' turns is round.
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch of the Thames flowing through Oxford is known by this name, so it is a river.

clue.text: Get away from best grid position, returning by end of race

indicators.note: the grid position word comes back, being read from right to left

parts.note: pole position is the front spot on the starting grid

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A driver quickly leaves pole position and comes back as the race ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns POLE into ELOP; 'end of' gives E from race.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off secretly, typically to marry, is a way of escaping.

clue.text: In primitive form, support race?

parts.note: to root for a team is to support it
stock means lineage or race, as in of farming stock

explanation.surface: Asking whether backing a race should be done in some basic, early way.
explanation.definitionFit: The underlying original from which offshoots or varieties derive is a primitive ancestral form.

clue.text: Present the same race

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same again
a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: An offer to put on an identical race once more.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is the abbreviation of ditto.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift handed over, often to charity, is a present.

clue.text: Starts to enter some privateer race in this Lotus car

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next six words are taken in turn

explanation.surface: A private team takes its sports car into a race.
explanation.walkthrough: A privateer is an independent racing team without works backing.
explanation.definitionFit: The wedge-shaped sports model built by Lotus, made famous in a Bond film, is one of its cars.
